source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: For an equation of the form Ax + B = Cx + D, identify A, B, C, and D in their positions and apply the formula x = (D - B)/(A - C).

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: B is the label that belongs on this item, so 'For an equation of the form Ax + B = Cx + D, identify A, B, C, and D' is answered as B rather than A.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: A still holds here even though The equation must be in, or be treated as, the stated Ax + B = Cx + D form is missing from the stem — on the item about For an equation of the form Ax + B = Cx + D, identify.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Divide to obtain x is what produces linear equation in Ax + B = Cx + D form, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about For an equation of the form Ax + B = Cx + D, identify.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The A rule also covers this: equations not expressible as Ax + B = Cx + D without prior rearrangement, so it is not an exception — on the item about For an equation of the form Ax + B = Cx + D, identify.

intelligence.enrichment: Equations generalised as Ax + B = Cx + D can be solved directly using Brahmagupta's formula x = (D - B)/(A - C), after the four numbers are identified from the two sides.
